newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Seng aims to be financial supermarket.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng aims to be financial supermarket.

text.p: Hang Seng Bank Ltd on Tuesday launched a computer-based investment planning service, SmartInvest, as part of efforts to become a provider of a full range of financial services to customers.

"We are focusing on more investment-related products as customer demand for such products increases," Chief Executive Alex Au said. "This is port of our plan to become a financial services supermarket offering one-stop banking."
Customers enter personal details and investment goals and preferences into the SmartInvest computer at retail branches, which then runs them through a series of tests to assess their risk appetite.

It then suggests several asset allocation models and points out a range of products such as savings and time deposits, stocks, gold and unit trusts offered by the bank or by six investment management companies.
Au noted that only a small percentage of the population currently had investments in stocks, pointing to huge potential for investment services.
Hang Seng also had strategy of boosting non-interest, fee-based income, he added.
